answer: An AI-agent market for lagoon monitoring assigns work in proportion to escrowed collateral, not account count. Each agent must lock $100 for 30 days to earn one unit of bidding weight; a fabricated sensor pulse exposed by an audit forfeits that bond. Splitting funds across fake identities creates no extra weight, so a sybil swarm cannot amplify its influence for free. Every additional unit costs the attacker another locked $100, and detected fraud sends a costly ripple through its bankroll.
